clusters.name: Your grandfather Amos's death, 1989–1990
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's death in July 1989, within the following months: your mother's worry over money in March 1988 and her distance from your father over it by May 1988 sit before the death; your brother's grades fell in November 1989, and your mother grew calmer once back at work by March 1990. The shifts in your mother's anxiety and the distance between your parents, followed by your brother's drop in functioning after the death, with your mother's anxiety easing as she returned to work, hold these events together as a reaction to the loss.

clusters.name: Your mother's breast cancer diagnosis, 1994–1996
clusters.reason: Around your mother's diagnosis in February 1995, within the year before and after: you developed migraines in March 1994, called your brother most nights in April 1994, then stopped returning his calls in June 1995 and stopped calling home in February 1996. Your shifts toward and then away from your brother, and your distance from your mother, frame the months around her diagnosis, with your own symptom rising as you left for college in September 1993 and your relationship moves intensifying through the diagnosis and after.
